title: D6_6a-N05 | Joint selection of winter/summer pressure tiers and one year-round acid dose
question_prompt:
D6_6a-N05 | Joint selection of winter/summer pressure tiers and one year-round acid dose

An SWRO plant may use different winter and summer pressures, while membrane area, PX configuration and the acid metering setpoint remain fixed year-round. Determine the minimum compliant pressure in each season, then use the two actual recoveries to find one common acid dose without over-dosing solely for the harsh season.

Engineering inputs and design boundary | Hard constraints and decision rule
Module area 70 m², PX efficiency 95%, A=4.0×10⁻¹² m/s/Pa and B=3.0×10⁻⁸ m/s. Winter is 15°C and 36 g/kg with 62–70 bar; summer is 31°C and 40 g/kg with 66–74 bar. Build a reproducible pressure grid for each season. | Each season must meet module water≥0.400 kg/s, NaCl≤350 mg/L, CP≤1.34; plant product≥0.043 m³/s and SEC≤3.00 kWh/m³. One common dose must keep both seasons at pH≥6.15 with all four SI≤0. Minimize seasonal pressures first, then the common dose.

Engineering dependency | Required engineering answer
Membrane performance and whole-plant performance must be evaluated for the same design identity. Only jointly feasible designs proceed to concentrate chemistry, whose recovery must inherit the actual membrane result. | 1 | Define a reproducible discrete search within the stated bounds.
Membrane performance and whole-plant performance must be evaluated for the same design identity. Only jointly feasible designs proceed to concentrate chemistry, whose recovery must inherit the actual membrane result. | 2 | Evaluate membrane and plant constraints without mixing design identities.
Membrane performance and whole-plant performance must be evaluated for the same design identity. Only jointly feasible designs proceed to concentrate chemistry, whose recovery must inherit the actual membrane result. | 3 | Transfer actual recovery into concentrate chemistry.
Membrane performance and whole-plant performance must be evaluated for the same design identity. Only jointly feasible designs proceed to concentrate chemistry, whose recovery must inherit the actual membrane result. | 4 | Show the controlling failure immediately outside the feasible boundary.
Membrane performance and whole-plant performance must be evaluated for the same design identity. Only jointly feasible designs proceed to concentrate chemistry, whose recovery must inherit the actual membrane result. | 5 | Report the final setting, decisive values and model limitations.

Boundary note
Do not substitute nominal recovery, mix outputs from different design packages, or average away a failed season/state. The answer must preserve engineering lineage from design identity to final chemistry verification.

tool_efficiency_rubric.reference_trajectory:
D6_6a-N05 | Tool efficiency (100 points)

Reference trajectory: 10 simulate_ro calls and 10 simulate_swro_system calls in parallel, followed by 10 equilibrate_feed calls on inherited recoveries. Efficiency means each call changes a feasibility boundary or ranking.

Stage | Tool | Calls | Key input | Key observation | State update | Next step
1 Metadata | describe_* | 0 | Units, species and valid parameter combinations | Lock common candidate identity | Create auditable search table | Fork
2A Parallel membrane | simulate_ro | 10 | Pressure, area, A/B, temperature and salinity | Water, NaCl, CP and actual recovery | Mark membrane-feasible IDs | Join
2B Parallel plant | simulate_swro_system | 10 | Same ID, plant area, ERD and pump settings | Product, SEC, CAPEX and LCOW | Mark plant-feasible IDs | Join
3 Join | — | 0 | Two aligned branch tables | Intersection and ranking boundary | Create chemistry shortlist | Transfer recovery
4 Serial chemistry | equilibrate_feed | 10 | Inherited recovery, ion analysis and dose/state | pH and mineral SI | Lock final feasible set | Check adjacent failure
5 Stop | — | 0 | Winner plus decisive failure evidence | No unresolved boundary | Report recommendation and limits | Stop

Hybrid-trajectory audit
Critical rule: both parallel branches must use the same design identity. Chemistry must inherit the exact actual recovery associated with that identity. Re-running chemistry with a rounded target recovery, or combining the membrane result of one package with the ERD/economics of another, breaks the trajectory even if the final recommendation happens to match.
